messages:
Sam: Quick dump from today's KV-slice experiment — tried aligning KV shards by layer (layerwise-locality) instead of the default tensor-slice across TP ranks. profiler shows a different comm/compute overlap profile.

Anya: can you paste the p50/p95/p99 + throughput numbers? curious if latency regressed for short requests.

Sam: p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=112ms, throughput down ~7% on steady-state but tail moved slightly lower for generation workloads that reuse KV heavily. (runs: tp=2 pp=1 dp=1, batch=8, seq=1024)

Mike: interesting. did you see any increase in all-reduce time or was it more point-to-point from KV syncs?

Sam: profiler snippet:
```
[GPU0] compute: 6.8ms
[GPU0] kv-serialize-send: 1.9ms
[GPU0] allreduce (params): 2.1ms
[GPU0] allreduce (kv-agg): 3.3ms
overlap: compute vs comm ~24%
```
KV slices now cause more peer sends (small messages) vs fewer larger sends when sharded by tensor-cols.

Lee: small-message overhead + PCIe/NCCL launch cost could explain throughput hit. also tuning kernels for shorter key lengths matters. did you try batching small KV sends into larger coalesced buffers?

Sam: yes — the next run coalesced layer keys per destination into a single send. results: throughput returned to baseline, p99 still slightly improved for cached queries. so coalescing + layerwise locality seems promising if we avoid many tiny sends.

Anya: what about pipeline parallel effects? with pp>1 does layerwise mapping cause hot spots where one PP rank holds many active layers' KV and gets overloaded?

Sam: good call — with pp=2 we saw imbalance. one PP rank became hotspot during decoding because many recent layers live there. imbalance led to queueing delays.

Mike: sounds like we need a placement policy that considers (1) TP/PP topology, (2) per-layer active-set probability, (3) coalescing budget. maybe a cost model: comm_cost = alpha + beta * size; prefer fewer sends even if slightly larger.

Lee: Agreed. propose quick experiments:
- placement A: layerwise but alternate assignment across PP stages to spread active layers
- placement B: hybrid (tensor-slice for early layers, layerwise for last n layers where KV reuse is high)
- placement C: layerwise + coalescing window of 50us

Sam: I'll run the matrix tomorrow. command I'm using:
```
./profiler --model redwood-7b --tp 2 --pp 2 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --kv-placement layerwise --coalesce 50us
```

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: recent commit b3a1f7 changed kernel launch strategy; p50 improved but p99 increased by 8% in nightly redwood-7b topo tests :eyes:

Anya: that bot alert aligns with what Sam saw. could be kernel selection that assumes larger contiguous KV chunks. we should add a microbenchmark that exercises many tiny KV sends to catch this.

Mike: I'll add a synthetic microbench to eng-runtime CI that runs on small-key workloads. also logging suggestion: add per-destination send size histogram to trace so we can tune coalescing thresholds.

Lee: action items:
- Sam: run placement A/B/C and post results (include per-gpu send-size histograms)
- Mike: add microbench + tracing hooks
- Anya: prototype cost model (alpha/beta) and simulate placement

Sam: thanks — posting results here once runs finish. :thumbsup:
